10.0.s.en: (1) I am the door of the sheep

10.0.0.en: The Lord Christ affirms here that He is the lawful owner and the only shepherd of His people. For the fold here is the Church, the sheep are His people, and the door is Christ, who is charged with the repentance and salvation of the souls of His people; in a comparison between Him and the priests of the Jews and the Pharisees, whom Christ considered thieves who had no compassion on the people but rather harmed them the more, attending to their own interests (see Ezek 34).

10.0.1.en: And the saying likewise applies to every unfaithful servant in the Church of God, who steals from the people of Christ for his own account, or steals with strange teaching, robbing Christ of His flock.

10.1.0.en: "The porter": a reference to the Holy Spirit, who opens hearts to the word and voice of the shepherd; and it is a continual work of the Holy Spirit. It can also be said that the porter is the faithful servant, who does not claim to be a shepherd but a porter, whose whole work is to open the door for the shepherd, meaning that he strives to bring Christ to people, without claiming for himself a greater role than this. As for the sheep, when they hear the voice of their faithful shepherd, whom they know well through daily companionship and friendship, and trust his leading of their lives, as he calls each one by its own name, as a sign of love, concern and special care... they go out after him to enjoy the sun of spiritual knowledge, and the air of the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

10.1.1.en: So do you, beloved, have this discernment of the voice of Christ in your life? He is always calling you, and speaking with you, longing for you to go out with Him into His spiritual pastures, that you may have satisfaction and enjoyment. So do not let anything of the voices of this world and its concerns occupy your ears from listening to the voice of your good Shepherd.

10.2.0.en: Since the sheep are reassured by the voice of their shepherd, which they know well, they follow behind him in complete surrender and absolute trust, for he alone knows where the good pastures are for his flock, and his flock looks to his feet, and follows his steps which lead it to the waters of eternal rest, imitating its leader in his humility, meekness, striving and sufferings, captivated by the love of his care for it. As for the stranger, he is the deceiving teacher, like the thief and the robber, for the flock that is aware and instructed within the Church distinguishes teaching foreign to the spirit of its Church and its Christ, and so it shrinks from this misleading teaching.

10.2.1.en: And therefore, beloved, being present within the atmosphere of the Church provides all of us with spiritual food free of deceit, and protects us from strange teachers who enter houses in the name of Christ, and are thieves and robbers who seek only to tear His body, that is, His Church, so do not listen to them... but flee from them.

10.3.0.en: The Jews did not understand Christ's meaning, especially the last comparison between the true shepherd and the stranger. Therefore, the Lord Christ begins in the coming verses to restate and explain, being long-suffering toward them.

10.4.0.en: "The door of the sheep": that is, I am the only entrance to the way of salvation, and there is no salvation outside my Body and my Blood. And likewise I am the only way out, from tribulation and pain, into the enjoyment of the spacious freedom of fellowship with God.

10.4.1.en: "All that ever came": of course He did not mean the prophets or the fathers, who were sent according to His choice and calling, but He means everyone who came before Him and claimed that he was the shepherd and teacher. This saying can also be applied to the scribes and Pharisees, but God's flock did not respond to their error. And St. Mark makes clear the difference between the voice of the true shepherd and the robbers, for "He taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes" (Mk 1:22). And Christ Himself described the scribes and Pharisees as robbers when He said of them: "Ye devour widows' houses" (Mt 23:14), that is, they took on the form of shepherds, but they were robbers. Therefore, the true people of God did not respond to their falseness. For just as a child can distinguish the voice of his father, so can the people of Christ with their great Shepherd.

10.5.0.en: "If any man enter in by me": the invitation stands, but God respects man's freedom. Salvation is offered to all people, but man may accept the gift of Christ, or reject it by his stubbornness and pride. For free salvation is conditioned on faith in the Shepherd, following Him, and striving with Him.

10.5.1.en: "Shall go in and out, and find pasture": the talk is about the fold, which is the Church, which provides its children with: first: union with Christ through Holy Communion.

10.5.2.en: Second: spiritual satisfaction through sound teaching.

10.5.3.en: Third: reassurance through the guidance of the fathers.

10.5.4.en: Fourth: freedom to set out in growth and in the true knowledge of God.

10.5.5.en: And the meaning of this is that life outside Christ and His Church is death.

10.5.6.en: My dear friend, Christ granted us life and bought it for us by His death for us all on the cross, and offered it to us and called us to it freely, and He seeks nothing but that we should enjoy all this, and have the better, "For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ" (ch. 1:17). All the revelations and prophets and appearances of the Old Testament become as nothing in comparison with what has been revealed to us in the person of Christ by His Incarnation and His offering of salvation to us. Indeed, the greatest and the best, my friend, is the indwelling of the true Holy Spirit of God within us. For on the day you were anointed with the Holy Myron, God dwelt within you and you became a temple for Him... So do you value this life and this better state, or is it the transient and false life that still allures you and distracts you from your Christ?

10.6.0.en: "The good shepherd": in (v. 1), we made clear the importance of the attribute of shepherd. But here, what is the goodness of Christ in comparison with shepherds such as Moses and David and others? These shepherds, in their turn, were themselves sheep whom God shepherds; but the goodness of Christ:

10.6.1.en: First: that He is the only Shepherd of shepherds, the Pantocrator, and the shepherding of no limited man rises to Christ's shepherding of His creation.

10.6.2.en: Second: the faithful shepherd may defend his flock and fight for it, but he does not risk his life, which is dearer than his flock... But Christ gave Himself for the salvation of all His flock, and it is the work of atoning redemption that no one can undertake except our Christ and good Shepherd...

10.6.3.en: Third: besides the work of redemption, the expression "the good shepherd" carries deep spiritual meanings... Christ is the One who takes care of preparing all that you need, and He is tender toward you in all your tribulations, and He is the defender of you against evil and danger... So if this is our Shepherd, why then do we worry and why do our daily worldly concerns trouble us?

10.6.4.en: Trust, beloved, in your loving Shepherd, who lays down His life for you.

10.7.0.en: A comparison that the Lord Christ presents, whose purpose is to show the extent of love in His shepherding of His flock, which He owns and redeems. For however great the faithfulness of the hireling, it will never rise to the love of the owner of the flock for his flock. The hireling's life is much more important than the sheep, so he flees if he senses the danger threatening his life. But the true owner of the flock takes up his cross and goes up on it by his own will alone, to die himself and give life to his people.

10.7.1.en: And the words here can be directed to the servants in the Church of Christ. The hireling servant is bound to those he serves by nothing but wages, that is, what he obtains of praise or self-gratification. But the faithful servant is for the sake of Christ, and out of fear for the flock of Christ, spares no effort... even his whole life is cheap for the sake of the Master's flock which was entrusted to him. And the Church is full of the lives of these faithful shepherds who also gave their lives for their people, such as St. Peter the Patriarch, the Seal of the Martyrs, who offered his life willingly, asking Christ that his blood be the end of the age of martyrdom from which the Coptic people suffered at the hands of the Romans.

10.8.0.en: After the Lord Christ presented the difference between the hireling and the owner of the flock, He returns to affirm the importance of His distinctive pastoral work as the good Shepherd; and He adds a new attribute that this shepherding includes, which is His knowledge of His own. Just as the shepherd knows his flock as a whole and by number, so He knows each one also by name (v. 3), and by his needs and tribulations, and even suffers with his suffering.

10.8.1.en: And this is a privilege enjoyed by all His children, unlike those who refuse to be within the Church, His fold, to whom the Shepherd says: "I never knew you" (Mt 7:23).

10.8.2.en: "And am known of mine": the knowledge of love, gratitude and thanksgiving from the sheep to their tender Shepherd, and the knowledge of experience of His strong arm and the work of His grace in our lives. For Christ has no equal or substitute for every soul that has enjoyed His friendship and care; He alone satisfies, and therefore the soul follows Him wherever He goes, and He is the source of its satisfaction and refreshment. Blessed are you, St. Paul, when you declare the depth of this knowledge, and say: "For I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him" (2 Tim 1:12).

10.9.0.en: Christ here likens His knowledge of His own to the knowledge that exists between Him and the Father. Just as the Father and the Son are in constant openness and communion, so nothing separates Christ from His flock. And as far as the flock is able, it too is in communion with its Master and Shepherd, the source of all its good... and the more a person increases in his love for Christ, the more his communion with Him increases, that is, the more his knowledge of Him increases...

10.9.1.en: So, beloved, the knowledge of God is available to all, because this is the desire of His heart and His good will. But there is a role for all of us in growing in the knowledge of God that satisfies every soul; and this role is that we give more of our time to spend with God, for whatever the occupations and obligations, they are not acceptable excuses before God. And the time we spend with God in prayer and reading is an investment in our life and our rest and our true peace.

10.10.0.en: "I lay down my life": since the love of the shepherd for his flock reached its end, self-giving and redemption come as a natural result of this faithful shepherding, and the reference here is to redemption, which is the goal for which Christ became incarnate, for there is no stronger proof than the death that Christ offers in His love for His people (ch. 1:13; ch. 15:13).

10.11.0.en: As the Lord Christ declares the mystery of redemption to the flock, He makes clear here that this redemption is not only for the people of Israel, for the true flock of Christ is everyone in the whole world who receives Him; He is not limited to the fold of Israel, because redemption and the cross were offered to all, and this is what the high priest prophesied in (ch. 11:52), that Christ would die to gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.

10.11.2.en: This phrase lays on all of us an obligation to seek out every soul far from Christ. For the servant and the true Christian man cannot rest while he knows that there are many who are still far from the Church of Christ, and he feels responsible toward these, exactly like his Christ, the great Shepherd. For if the lost sheep come to know the voice of the great Shepherd, they too become part of His flock, following Him wherever He goes.

10.12.0.en: "Therefore doth my Father love me": the love between the Father and the Son is an eternal love that does not depend on anything, but Christ draws attention here to His giving of Himself as a sacrifice of redemption for the whole world, and this sacrifice the Father accepts with joy and love.

10.13.0.en: And lest it be thought that the Son's obedience to the Father diminishes His worth, or His equality with the Father, Christ continues His discourse, making clear His authority and absolute will in the process of death and redemption; for the will of the Father and the Son is one and equal in the redemption of man, the Father by planning and the Son by carrying out. Therefore, Christ focuses here on His authority, that it is He who lays down His life of His own will in order to take it again, that is, He is the One going to death to crush it, and death has no authority over Him. And the word "take it again" means the Resurrection, that is, He receives back His spirit that tasted death in the body, and Satan has no authority to seize the human spirit of the Lord Christ, which is subject to the will of the Son alone. "This commandment have I received of my Father": the commandment here refers to the Father's plan in the salvation of man, for Christ accepted this plan by His own will, and not by compulsion or coercion.

10.13.1.en: Beloved... does the humility of the heavenly Son toward the Father, who is of one essence with Him, not strike you, emptying Himself, and offering Himself, with all love, to buy you with His holy, precious blood? Why then do high self-regard and the pride of the soul still pursue us, and are we deceived by their false appearances? Have we not yet learned from our God?!

10.14.0.en: As usual (ch. 7:43; ch. 9:16), a division of opinion occurs among the Jews for two reasons:

10.14.1.en: The first: their not understanding what He said, not perceiving the spiritual dimensions of His words.

10.14.2.en: The second: their enmity toward Christ as a result of the effect of His words on others, so it was easier for them to accuse Him of blasphemy and of following Satan.

10.14.3.en: But a group remained who did not agree with the former in their opinion... for they had not yet forgotten the miracle of the man born blind, and brought it forward here as evidence denying Christ any relationship with the kingdom of darkness.

10.15.0.en: St. John interrupts here the discourse of the Lord Christ about the flock and the good Shepherd, to add for us the dimension of time and place of this discourse, for this Feast of Dedication is a national and spiritual feast, added by Judas Maccabeus as a memorial of the cleansing of the Temple from the Greek occupation, which defiled the Temple and killed more than forty thousand of the Jews. And the time was winter, about the middle of December. And since Solomon's porch was the only roofed porch, the Lord Christ took shelter in it from the cold and the rain.

10.16.0.en: All the Fathers and interpreters agree that the purpose of the question was not faith in Christ and following Him, but a new attempt to catch Him in a word, so that they might accuse Him of blasphemy, especially what they asked of Him, that He declare this openly, that is, before all the crowds, so that they would have a complaint against Him before the council of the leaders of the Jews on the one hand, and before the Roman state on the other, because the declaration that He is the Christ implicitly includes that He is the King of the Jews, their liberator from the Romans. Therefore, Christ's answer came indirectly, but He did not deny the truth about Himself, but pointed to the miraculous works that He had done, and which no one but He could do. And the Lord used the same reply, that His works bear witness to Him (ch. 5:36; 9:4; 10:

10.17.0.en: Christ presents here the reason for the Jews' unbelief in Him, whether in His words or His works. And this reason is that they are not of His sheep, or of God; for man's pride prevents him from listening to the voice of God, and this is what the scribes and Pharisees suffered. But the simple and humble people received Christ's word and rejoiced in it. And the phrase "as I said unto you" is a reminder from Christ of what He said in (vv. 4, 14) and also (ch. 8:47).

10.18.0.en: A repetition of what came in (vv. 4, 14), and the purpose is to affirm the same spiritual meanings in God's knowledge of His own, and their recognition of His voice.

10.19.0.en: "And I give unto them eternal life": a very special gift enjoyed by the flock of Christ alone, which is the gift of the inheritance of eternal life. But how does He give them this eternal life? The answer is through what He had also spoken of before:

10.19.1.en: (1) Birth from Baptism and the Holy Spirit, in His discourse with Nicodemus (ch. 3:5).

10.19.2.en: (2) Faith in the only-begotten Son (ch. 3:16, 36; ch. 6:47).

10.19.3.en: (3) Partaking of His most holy Body and precious Blood (ch. 6:54).

10.19.4.en: (4) Continual following of Christ, striving, and acceptance of tribulations (ch. 12:25).

10.19.5.en: "They shall never perish... neither shall any man pluck them":

10.19.6.en: How sweet are these words, which spread reassurance in the soul and drive away our doubts about the salvation of our souls... Yes, beloved God, we believe that we have eternal life in You alone, and You are our keeper and protector. And how could we not be saved, when You have granted us free salvation in Baptism, and the forgiveness of sins in the sacrament of the most holy Communion, and the sacrament of repentance and confession? We are reassured, my Lord. But grant us the spirit of striving against sins until we complete the salvation of our souls...

10.20.0.en: In (v. 28), the Lord says: "Neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand," and here He says: "No man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand," and this is proof and evidence that the hand of the Father and the Son are one in ability, power, and also will. Therefore the important declaration came in (v. 30) "I and my Father are one," which is one of the strongest verses proving the divinity of Christ and the equality of the Son with the Father. As for the expression "My Father, which gave them me," its meaning is that from eternity, before the foundation of the world, all creation was given to the Son, for He is its Creator (ch. 1:3), and He is its Redeemer (ch. 10:15), and He is its protector and ruler (ch. 10:28).

10.20.1.en: "Is greater than all": whatever the attempts of Satan to snatch and scatter the flock of God, God is stronger, and His protection is unlimited.

10.20.2.en: So do we trust, my beloved, in the strong hand of God, and His protection of His Church, or do we still worry about this and that? Beloved... you are in the hands of your heavenly Father, enjoying a surpassing protection through which you can be victorious over the power of the wicked adversary. So do not belittle the strong hand of God that crushes all evils, but come, let us sing with Solomon the wise, saying: "The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

10.21.s.en: (5) The accusation against Christ of blasphemy

10.21.0.en: The strong declaration that the Lord Christ made of His oneness with the Father angered the Jews, because of their failure to grasp all the previous sayings and wonders, which no man performs. So they tried to stone Him, considering all that He said about His relationship with the Father to be blasphemy. And instead of listening, understanding and taking in the good works that Christ had done, their eyes and hearts were closed to them, and nothing remained but the desire to kill Him. Beloved, do not we too often forget, especially in time of tribulation and trial, all that God has done with us of good and miracles throughout the years of our life, and listen only to the voice of the enemy of good, who casts doubt on God's care for His children?!

10.21.1.en: Do we not wrong God with us at that time?

10.21.2.en: O my beloved God... forgive us our boldness and our wronging of You, and do not make us like those whose eyes were blinded to You and to Your goodness.

10.22.0.en: A person may endure wrong for the sake of God, and not defend himself. But the charge of blasphemy is the only one that the Christian does not accept against himself, because accepting it would mean denying God. And here, Christ defends Himself against this false charge, using the Law itself. For the Law called Moses a god to his brother Aaron (Ex 4:16), and in (Ps 82:6) it says: "I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High," and the Law is true and cannot be broken. So if the Law has called certain men gods, and this was not considered blasphemy, then even if I were only a man... I did not blaspheme when I used the same designation for myself, that is, it is a designation that has a reference among you... And the second objection that the Lord presented is stronger, because He declares about Himself that He is not an ordinary man (v. 36), for He is the Holy One of God, that is, the One appointed from eternity as Christ for the salvation of mankind, and sent by His Incarnation into the world. For all who preceded Him were called gods, because the word of God came to them (v. 35). But He is the Word of God Himself (ch. 1:1), so how can He not be God by nature? Therefore, He is the Son of God, and He is also God, and He and the Father are one.

10.23.0.en: As for the third proof that Christ presents against the accusation of blasphemy, it is the works themselves, which were already referred to in (ch. 5:36; 9:3-5; 10:35, 38; 14:

10.23.1.en: 10-12). And it is that the works He does are all divine works, which no man has ever done; from feeding the crowds, and raising the sick man of Bethsaida, to healing the man born blind. And these works alone, even without your listening to my words, are sufficient for you to believe when I said to you: "I and my Father are one," because I am in the Father and the Father in me.

10.24.0.en: The events end with all that the Lord said not convincing the Jews, but they sought to seize Him in anger, either to stone Him outside, or to bring Him to the leaders for trial. But Christ, since His hour had not yet come, "no man laid hands on him" (ch. 7:44), and He passed through their midst without their seizing Him (ch. 8:59).

10.25.0.en: That is, to the east of the Jordan, where the Lord Jesus was baptized by the Baptist, and this region is known as Perea (Mt 19:1), in which the Lord Christ spent the last 4 months of His Incarnation, that is, from December until the Passover before His crucifixion. And Christ's presence in that place drew to Him many of the crowds who accepted faith in their simplicity; and the comparison these simple people made between the Lord and John the Baptist, who did not perform a single miracle, shows us that Christ performed signs and miracles during the period of His stay there. And these miracles, in addition to John's witness to Him, were a cause of the faith of many. The raising of Lazarus
